category.name: Websites and CMS
category.description: Build websites and manage published content.
category.audience: Individuals, small businesses, publishers, agencies and organizations maintaining websites.
category.audienceRationale: Website publishing serves personal, commercial, nonprofit and institutional needs across industries.

pricing.note: Paid Light plan; localized rendering includes GST and conflicting currency cues, so a reliable USD entry price was not established. Free SaaS plan also exists.
Basic is paid; page renders $25/$19 without sufficiently clear currency and billing mapping. USD amount unresolved.
Basic site plan: USD 15 per site/month billed yearly; lacks CMS. Premium with CMS starts at USD 25/site/month billed yearly. Workspace seats/add-ons separate.

oss.name: WordPress
oss.classificationReason: Tier A for community WordPress core: standard publishing, users and themes available without licensing fees. Commercial plugins/themes are separate products, not core gates. WordPress.com is a distinct Automattic managed service linked by WordPress.org; its plan limits do not apply to self-hosted core. GitHub distribution repository mirrors SVN; wordpress-develop is also a mirror used for contribution workflow.

health.rsx: Shared authenticated analysis pending; GitHub metadata fallback used.

serviceLimitations: Self-hosting requires infrastructure and maintenance; optional commercial plugins/themes/services may cost extra.

oss.name: Drupal
oss.classificationReason: Tier A for Drupal core: project explicitly provides free CMS functionality without licensing fees; modules/themes and vendor platforms separate. Hosting directory lists independent providers, not a Drupal Association managed service. GitHub repository is a mirror; canonical development is on Drupal.org GitLab. Pinned core/LICENSE.txt contains GPL v2; official licensing policy explicitly grants version 2 or later.

health.rsx: Shared authenticated analysis pending; GitHub metadata fallback used.

serviceLimitations: Hosting, implementation and optional vendor services are separate costs; contributed modules are outside core assessment.

oss.name: Ghost
oss.classificationReason: Tier A for self-hosted Ghost: official comparison explicitly says product features are identical. Ghost(Pro) hosting plan gates do not gate self-hosted software. Social web and analytics require separate services and supported deployment setup.

health.rsx: Shared authenticated analysis pending; GitHub metadata fallback used.

serviceLimitations: Self-hosting requires operations and email delivery services.
Hosted ActivityPub access for self-hosters has follower and interaction limits; independent self-hosting available.

alternatives.migrationNotes: Suitable for business sites and blogs using WordPress themes and publishing. Wix site runtime cannot transfer to another host; rebuild layout and business integrations, migrate content separately. Optional plugins may be needed.
Squarespace exports WordPress XML for selected pages and one blog. Store/portfolio pages, styles, custom CSS and several block types do not export; rebuild design and integrations.

Best for a publication/blog. Built-in Squarespace XML migrator imports posts/pages and converts categories to tags; review redirects and rebuild design. Broader store/scheduling workflows need separate solutions.

WordPress supplies a theme/plugin CMS rather than Webflow Designer. Webflow CMS collections export separately as CSV; code export omits CMS runtime, forms and ecommerce. Map content and rebuild templates/integrations.

For structured CMS projects with developer implementation. Webflow CSV content needs mapping into Drupal; Migrate provides APIs/base implementations, not a verified automatic Webflow importer. Rebuild templates and backend behavior.

uncertainties: Wix and Squarespace USD entry prices unresolved because localized/dynamic price rendering did not establish unambiguous figures.
WordPress and Drupal GitHub latest-release endpoints return 404; null release fields describe GitHub mirrors, not absence of upstream releases.
